The `blowhorn auth` commands. Each one's `--help` prints the same text.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`auth anonymous-usage-stats`](#blowhorn-auth-anonymous-usage-stats) | Show or set whether your account shares anonymous usage data for product improvement. |

## blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats

Show or set whether your account shares anonymous usage data for product improvement.

Reads and writes anonymousUsageStats in your Blowhorn account's preferences (GET /api/identity/users/profile, PUT /api/identity/users/preferences with that one field, so no other preference changes). It belongs to the account, so every computer you use Blowhorn on follows it. Not set reads as on. Usage data is anonymous counts of what Blowhorn does; it never carries a post's text, a message, a credential or the contents of a page Blowhorn drives. Failure reports are a separate setting in the desktop app. With no flag it reads your account and always exits 0: signed out or unreachable, it reports the setting last read for this account (or on) and says why. `--on` and `--off` save the setting and exit 1 when your account cannot be written. `--dry-run` reads and sends nothing.

```text
blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--on` | boolean | `false` | Share anonymous usage data for product improvement (saved to your account). |
| `--off` | boolean | `false` | Stop sharing anonymous usage data (saved to your account). |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn auth`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats
blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats --off
blowhorn auth anonymous-usage-stats --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn auth login

Sign in to Blowhorn at https://cloud.blowhorn.ai in your browser.

Opens https://cloud.blowhorn.ai, where you sign in or create an account and allow the Blowhorn app, then returns here and keeps the token in the macOS Keychain (elsewhere a file only you can read beside cloud.yaml). It uses Blowhorn's native client sign-in: the browser answers on 127.0.0.1 with a one-time code this command redeems with a PKCE verifier; there is no client secret, and the token is never printed. After sign-in it reads your plan once; an account without a Blowhorn plan is sent straight to https://cloud.blowhorn.ai to start the beta. `--no-browser` prints the sign-in address instead of opening it; `--json` opens no browser either, its first line names the address to open (the desktop app runs `--no-browser` `--json` and opens it itself). `--dry-run` names where it would sign in and opens, waits for and saves nothing.

```text
blowhorn auth login [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--sign-up` | boolean | `false` | Open https://cloud.blowhorn.ai to create a new account instead of signing in; it comes back the same way. |
| `--no-browser` | boolean | `false` | Print the sign-in address and wait for the answer on 127.0.0.1 without opening a browser (`--json` implies it). |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn auth`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth login` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth login` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn auth login
blowhorn auth login --sign-up
blowhorn auth login --no-browser --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn auth logout

Sign out of Blowhorn and clear the local entitlement attestation cache.

Removes the token `blowhorn auth login` saved (Keychain item ai.blowhorn.cloud-token), the account it wrote to cloud.yaml (organization_id, display_name and the account facts), the process cache and the Keychain attestation item (ai.blowhorn.entitlement.v2). Unset `BLOWHORN_CLOUD_TOKEN` in the shell if it was exported.

```text
blowhorn auth logout [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn auth`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |

Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth logout` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

## blowhorn auth status

Show whether Blowhorn credentials and an entitlement attestation are present.

Reports token configured (never the token value), organization id, api_base, enforcement mode (`BLOWHORN_ENTITLEMENT`), and a summary of the last Feature read. Live, it first re-reads the signed-in account from Blowhorn (name, photo, organizations, plan) into cloud.yaml and follows the organization your Blowhorn session in the browser has selected; `BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION` still wins when set, and the plan read and shown is that organization's. `--offline` answers from presence checks only: it reads no saved secret, so macOS shows no Keychain prompt, and it makes no network request (the desktop app runs it at launch). Exits 3 when this computer is not signed in: no token, a token Blowhorn refused, or Blowhorn could not be reached. `--offline` exits 3 only when no token is configured.

```text
blowhorn auth status [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--offline` | boolean | `false` | Check only whether a token and a saved plan are present; read no secret and make no request. |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn auth`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth status` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn auth status` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn auth status
blowhorn auth status --json
blowhorn auth status --offline --json
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.

## blowhorn auth switch-organization

Switch the signed-in account to another of its organizations.

Makes `ORGANIZATION_ID` the organization the account's Blowhorn session has selected, with the same write Blowhorn's and Meshery's own organization switchers send (PUT /api/identity/users/preferences, selectedOrganizationId), so the browser and this computer follow it. `ORGANIZATION_ID` must be one of the account's organizations ('auth status `--json`' lists them as account.organizations). Then reports what `auth status` reports, read live for the new organization. `BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION`, when set, still names the organization this computer reports. `--dry-run` checks the id and sends nothing.

```text
blowhorn auth switch-organization [OPTIONS] ORGANIZATION_ID
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ORGANIZATION_ID` | yes | The id of one of the account's organizations (auth status `--json`: account.organizations). |

Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
